notes.3: αἴρεσθαι ('to be raised') may mean 'to have an erection' here; the sense is uncertain. Thapsia is a plant whose juice blisters the skin. After 'juice' the edition prints a cancelled writing in double brackets (χειλῶι?), not translated. The words broken across lines 3/4 and 7/8 (νε|κροῦ, κυνό|δηκτον) are broken the same way in the English. Lines 2–3: τὸ αἰδοῖον has no possessive; the practitioner's own member may be meant, the woman being the trick's victim.

nodes.text: For someone in the bath to be raised up: of a de-
ad dog, crush the tick onto the loins.
To play a trick on a woman: with the juice of thapsia
For a fight to break out at a sym[p]osium: a dog-
bitten stone, throw it into the middle.
